label: <DEL> step of short sequences starting with g that contain q/y/p
explanation: A very sparse feature (434 activations in 1M sequences). 99% of its activation mass is at the delimiter step (t == L); it essentially never fires during the original or copy phases. It is almost entirely restricted to L = 4-6 (L=5 is the peak, none at L=3, close to none at L>=7). The first original token is the main cue: 82% of mass comes from sequences starting with g (lift 22x), with small contributions from v, e, 3, u. Within that, activation depends on how many q, y, p (and to a lesser degree v) tokens appeared, especially near the end (prev_tok y has lift 15x). The top example, g v q p y <DEL>, has all of them. It behaves like a conjunction-plus-threshold: delimiter & first g & L<=6 covers 80% of mass, but only about 2% of those steps fire. Also requiring >=2 of q/y/p gets dev precision 0.18, recall 0.39 and mass recall 0.57. Magnitude rises with more q/y/p tokens and with first token g, but the exact firing rule could not be captured as a clean predicate.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=y (+2.75), orig0=g (+2.74), orig2=q (+2.68), phase=1 & out_tok=g (+2.58), phase=1 & out_tok=v (+2.15), prev2_tok=y (+1.83). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.23), in_count=1 (-1.52), recall_idx=-1 (-1.35), to_go=2 (-1.26).
